subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw contain Playwright CDP assertion failures inside the browser plugin with a narrow classifier/reconnect path, or pursue broader browser process isolation before changing the fatal Gateway fallback?
rationale: The source shows a real in-process fatal path, but the safe fix shape crosses browser plugin ownership, Gateway process-fatal policy, and possible child-process isolation; automation should not choose that recovery boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Browser-owned containment first
options.body: Add a narrow browser plugin handler or CDP session quarantine/reconnect path for proven Playwright CDP assertions while leaving unknown process-level rejections fatal.

options.title: Design subprocess isolation
options.body: Treat this as a larger architecture item that moves browser/CDP operations out of the main Gateway process before accepting a code fix.

options.title: Wait for live proof only
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until a maintainer or reporter reproduces the exact CRSession stack on current main.

recommendation.title: Browser-owned containment first
recommendation.body: Add a narrow browser plugin handler or CDP session quarantine/reconnect path for proven Playwright CDP assertions while leaving unknown process-level rejections fatal.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across both the process-level unhandled-rejection boundary and browser/CDP runtime ownership.
